problem.title: First and Last Message per Match
problem.prompt: You are analyzing conversation patterns in a dating app. The `match_messages` table stores all messages sent between matched users. Each match is identified by `match_id`, and messages are timestamped. Write a query that returns one row per match showing: the match_id, the content of the FIRST message sent (earliest timestamp), and the content of the LAST message sent (latest timestamp) in that conversation. Order the results by match_id ascending. Note: some matches may have only one message, and you must correctly identify the true last message in each partition, not just the current row's value.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE match_messages (message_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, match_id INT NOT NULL, sent_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, message_content TEXT NOT NULL);
problem.example_input_data: INSERT INTO match_messages (match_id, sent_at, message_content) VALUES (101, '2024-01-10 14:30:00', 'Hey! Nice profile'), (101, '2024-01-10 14:45:00', 'Thanks! How was your weekend?'), (101, '2024-01-10 15:20:00', 'Pretty good, went hiking'), (102, '2024-01-11 09:00:00', 'Hi there!'), (102, '2024-01-11 09:15:00', 'Hello! Love your travel photos'), (102, '2024-01-11 10:30:00', 'Want to grab coffee sometime?'), (103, '2024-01-12 18:00:00', 'Hey, matched with you at the concert!'), (103, '2024-01-12 18:05:00', 'Yes! That was a great show');
example_output_rows: Hey, matched with you at the concert!
Yes! That was a great show
test_expected_rows: We should take them to the park together

composite_moves: window FIRST_VALUE OVER (PARTITION BY match_id ORDER BY sent_at)
window LAST_VALUE OVER (PARTITION BY match_id ORDER BY sent_at ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
DISTINCT to collapse to one row per match

hints: Use window functions to access the first and last values within each match partition.
FIRST_VALUE works with the default frame, but LAST_VALUE requires an explicit frame clause to see beyond the current row.
Specify `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING` in your LAST_VALUE window to get the true last message in each match, then use DISTINCT to collapse to one row per match_id.
problem.answer_key: SELECT DISTINCT match_id, FIRST_VALUE(message_content) OVER (PARTITION BY match_id ORDER BY sent_at) AS first_message, LAST_VALUE(message_content) OVER (PARTITION BY match_id ORDER BY sent_at ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_message FROM match_messages ORDER BY match_id;

_meta.scenario: a dating app tracking mutual matches and messaging engagement

user_solution:
/* notes */

SELECT
    DISTINCT
    match_id,
    FIRST_VALUE(message_content) OVER (PARTITION BY match_id ORDER BY sent_at
                                        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS first_message,
    LAST_VALUE(message_content) OVER (PARTITION BY match_id ORDER BY sent_at
                                        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_message
FROM match_messages
ORDER BY 1;
